'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Russian invasion of Ukraine (2022–present)|Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
**[[2022–2023 Western Russia attacks]]
***[[2023 Saint Petersburg bombing]]
****Russian pro-[[government of Russia|government]] war correspondent [[Vladlen Tatarsky]] is killed by a [[bomb]]ing at a café in [[Saint Petersburg]] owned by oligarch [[Yevgeny Prigozhin]]. Sixteen others are injured. [https://tass.ru/proisshestviya/17429999 (TASS)]
**[[Attacks on civilians in the Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
***[[Russian Armed Forces|Russian forces]] shell [[Kostiantynivka]], [[Donetsk Oblast]], killing six [[civilian]]s and injuring eight others, according to the [[Ukrainian government]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/ukraine-says-least-three-killed-six-wounded-russian-shelling-east-country-2023-04-02/ (Reuters)]
*[[Kivu conflict]]
**[[Military of South Sudan|South Sudanese troops]] arrive in [[Goma]], [[Democratic Republic of the Congo]], becoming the fourth country to join a [[coalition]] of [[peacekeeping]] missions to fight [[insurgencies]]. [https://english.news.cn/20230402/cf6d51c0abea44d48169ccdc66cd71ea/c.html (Xinhua)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*At least 21 people are dead and others are missing after a [[landslide]] in the locality of Bolowa (Bulwa village/[[Masisi Territory]]), [[North Kivu]], [[Democratic Republic of Congo]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2023/4/3/at-least-21-killed-several-missing-in-eastern-dr-congo-landslide (Al Jazeera)]
*Fifteen people are killed after two [[Gold mining|Gold pit]]s are [[flood]]ed in [[Cibitoke Province]], [[Burundi]]. [https://apnews.com/article/burundi-artisanal-gold-mining-flooding-deaths-001286ffbb1abff19ceee0e4ba74403a (AP)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2023 Andorran parliamentary election]]
**[[Andorrans]] head to the polls to elect the 28 members of the [[Parliament of Andorra|parliament]]. [https://www.elperiodico.com/es/internacional/20230401/claves-politicas-sociales-entender-elecciones-andorra-2a-85234889 (elPeriódico)]
*[[2023 Bulgarian parliamentary election]]
**[[Bulgarians]] head to the polls to elect the 240 members of the [[Parliament of Bulgaria|parliament]]. Exit polls show former Prime Minister [[Boyko Borisov]]'s party [[GERB]] narrowly defeating former Prime Minister [[Kiril Petkov]]'s party [[We Continue the Change]] by 0.2%. [https://www.dw.com/en/bulgaria-goes-to-polls-for-fifth-time-in-2-years/a-65206438 (DW)]
*[[2023 Finnish parliamentary election]]
**[[Finns]] head to the polls to elect the 200 members of the [[parliament of Finland|parliament]]. Centre-right [[National Coalition Party]] wins the most votes at 20.7%, while the ruling [[Social Democratic Party of Finland|Social Democratic Party]] places third with 19.9%. [https://www.euronews.com/2023/04/02/tight-race-in-prospect-as-polls-open-in-finlands-parliamentary-election (Euronews 1)] [https://www.euronews.com/2023/04/02/finlands-national-coalition-party-set-to-win-election-public-broadcaster-says (Euronews 2)]
*[[2023 Montenegrin presidential election]]
**Former economic minister [[Jakov Milatović]] defeats incumbent [[Milo Đukanović]] to become the new [[President of Montenegro|President]] of [[Montenegro]], with 60.1% of the vote.  [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/montenegro-holds-run-off-presidential-election-2023-04-02/ (Reuters)]
*[[2024 Republican Party presidential primaries]]
**Former [[Governor of Arkansas|Arkansas Governor]] [[Asa Hutchinson]] announces [[Asa Hutchinson 2024 presidential campaign|his campaign]] for the [[2024 United States presidential election]] during an interview with [[ABC News (United States)|ABC News]]. [https://abcnews.go.com/Politics/abc-news-exclusive-former-arkansas-gov-asa-hutchinson/story?id=98238115 (ABC News)]
